statement: Byrnes' proof loses effectivity at exactly one step: the converse direction of Lemma 4 ('Finally, suppose that k in Q(A). Since any A_{m,n} is finite, we can find an M and N such that...'), which extracts M and N from the bare finiteness of the set of positions with g-value k. That step is the sole source of T(A,k) and hence of W(A,k), and W(A,k) is the ONLY non-computable term in the final bound. The Lemma 9 pigeonhole is explicit: p_{A,k} <= 4^(|A|+k) p and N_{A,k} <= N + 4^(|A|+k) p.

statement: Zeilberger's exposition is a DIFFERENT proof of the 3-row case and contains no non-effective step. Its pigeonhole is over the explicitly counted state space S_a = (I_a; L_{a-1},...,L_{a-M}), giving N(r) + period(r) <= p_r (M_r+1)^(M_r) with M_r a bound on p-q below r and p_r = lcm{period(c) : c<r}. An effective Byrnes for 3-row Chomp therefore needs only (Z1) an explicit bound on max_q (f(q,r)-q), and (Z2) a bound on the lcm of the periods below r.

statement: NOVELTY: Hegarty-Larsson (INTEGERS 6 (2006) #A03) Theorem 3.3 gives only the ASYMPTOTIC DENSITY (L,l) of greedy difference permutations, with NO error term: the proof states the convergence rate is determined by M+,M-,S and "We omit any further details". Their Conjecture 5.1 (and 6.4) is EXACTLY the strip-bound statement we need: there exists c=c_{m,p} with pi_{m,p}(n) within c of floor(nL) or floor(nl). This is stated OPEN in their paper. So the strip bound |A029902(n)-a n|<=K is not in the literature; it is (morally) H&L Conjecture 5.1 specialised, and H&L machinery does NOT directly deliver an error term. Also: a=1+sqrt2/2 and b=1+sqrt2 satisfy 1/a+1/b=1 exactly (Beatty pair) and b=sqrt2*a exactly.

statement: SELF-SIMILARITY (exact form of the renormalization fixed point). For the stale rows A029902 and a=1+sqrt(2)/2, b=1+sqrt(2) (=sqrt(2)*a exactly, Beatty pair 1/a+1/b=1), the discrepancy D(x)=#{A029902<=x}-x/a satisfies D(x)+D(bx) in {-1,0,1} for every integer x with bx<=50000. Equivalently #{A029902<=x}+#{A029902<=bx}=2x+{-1,0,1}. This is the self-similarity the Friedman-Landsberg picture predicts, in exact (not merely asymptotic) form: the stale set is invariant under x->bx up to a discrepancy of magnitude <=1.

statement: NEGATIVE RESULT: the stale/live indicator word w(n)=[n is a stale constant A029901] over n=1..50000 is NOT Sturmian and NOT of low (linear) factor complexity. Factor complexity c(k)=#{distinct length-k factors} grows superlinearly: c(2)=4 (Sturmian would be 3), c(5)=22, c(10)=234, c(20)=7579, and reaches the maximal possible value min(2^k, N-k+1) by k~40. So any proof route requiring the word to be Sturmian/balanced/morphic-of-low-complexity is dead: A029901 has essentially maximal subword complexity while still having bounded discrepancy (C0016). This is the 'chaos' in Zeilberger's title: bounded discrepancy coexists with high complexity.

evidence: exact integer computation N(x)+N(floor(bx))-2x over x=1..20710 (bx<=50000): values {-1:4955, 0:14114, 1:1641}, nothing else. Iteration identity D(x)=e(x)-D(bx) verified symbolically; alternating-sum formal solution noted (needs the tail to vanish, i.e. D bounded at infinity, which is circular but pinpoints the structure).
statement: EXACT INTEGER FORM + ITERATION. With N(x)=#{A029902<=x}, the self-similarity is the exact integer relation N(x)+N(floor(b x)) = 2x + e(x), e(x) in {-1,0,1} (no floating point; x/a + bx/a = 2x exactly since 1/a+1/b=1... correction: x/a+bx/a = x(1+b)/a = 2x). Rewriting in D(x)=N(x)-x/a: D(x)+D(floor(bx))=e(x). Iterating the cocycle gives the formal solution D(x) = sum_{k>=0} (-1)^k e(floor(b^k x)) (plus a vanishing tail), so boundedness of D is EQUIVALENT to boundedness of these alternating base-b digit sums. This shows the self-similarity is a cocycle/substitution equation: it does NOT by itself force D bounded (adversarial e could make the alternating sum grow), so the mex structure must supply the self-consistency of e. The e-values are NOT arbitrary: e(x) in {-1,0,1} is determined by D, and the actual distribution is {0:14114, -1:4955, 1:1641} for x with bx<=50000.

evidence: counterexample verified symbolically: k=floor(log_b x), D(x)=(-1)^k k, then D(x)+D(b x)=(-1)^{k+1} in {-1,1} and D unbounded. So bounded e does not imply bounded D.
statement: NEGATIVE RESULT (kills Route A as stated): the cocycle D(x)+D(floor(bx)) in {-1,0,1} does NOT by itself force D bounded. Explicit counterexample: D(x)=(-1)^k * k with k=floor(log_b x) satisfies D(x)+D(bx) in {-1,1} for all x while D is unbounded. Therefore the mex structure of A029901/A029902 must supply the self-consistency of e(x)=N(x)+N(floor(bx))-2x; the self-similarity is a CONSEQUENCE of the structure, not a sufficient condition. Route A needs the additional constraint that e is itself generated by the greedy mex rule (D(x)-D(x-1) = [x in A902] - 1/a, and A902 is the mex-determined set).
